parentReviewReason: Artifact hash verification does not validate semantic extraction. The reported first two minable sites are both labelled coal with size 32; ore/height/attempt mappings are visibly shifted, and claimed dungeon cobble/mossy raw IDs 27/28 conflict with block identity. Per-site numbers were inferred from unrelated preceding literals without proven control/data flow. No semantic rule, count, range, distribution or class-role mapping in this candidate is approved for enforcement until independently re-derived.
implementationNote: Factual research evidence only. No mod, build, config, upstream or game file was edited and no game was launched. Nothing here authorises recreating terrain, noise or climate algorithms: Moderner Beta remains the terrain authority.

scopeAndConstraints.objective: Hash-bound primary Beta 1.7.3 client evidence for bounded generation-content compatibility: positive identification of the Block registry class and the chunk POPULATE/decoration classes, ore attempt/vein-size/height numbers, and dungeon/lake/tree/flower presence.

scopeAndConstraints.methodsAccepted: Only numeric facts, class/method paths and instruction offsets are recorded. No proprietary source, bytecode dump, texture or asset is copied into the repository.

rawConstructorOffsetVsNumericRegistryId.warning: The int literal passed to a block constructor is the RAW registry id used as an array index at class-initialisation time. Do not reuse it as a saved/serialised id without separate verification.
evidence: uu.<clinit> builds the block registry in ascending raw id order starting at raw id 1 (air has no instance at raw id 0) and writes each into the 256-entry uu.m array

the second literal of a block construction is an unrelated TEXTURE index, not a second id: e.g. the ore-family entries carry texture indices 32, 33, 34 (uu.H literals [14, 32], uu.I literals [15, 33], uu.J literals [16, 34])
item ids are a separate registry and are known to be offset from constructor arguments (handoff: bucket raw 69 -> saved 325); no item-registry claim is made here
KNOWN PRIOR REJECTION applies: research/beta173-availability.json must not be used to cross-check these ids

rawConstructorOffsetVsNumericRegistryId.fieldNameMappingCaveat: Field names quoted with the ids above come from the `new X; ...; putstatic field` assignment sequence in uu.<clinit>. During this task at least one such sequence-derived mapping (uu.ax) was found to be off by one entry, so the field NAME to raw ID pairing should be treated as MEDIUM confidence while the constructor LITERALS themselves are HIGH confidence. The ore rules below therefore key on the literals and on the observed texture-index family (32-34 = ores, 48-51 = diamond/redstone), not on field names.

orePopulationRules.callShape: `new fl` -> `dup` -> `getstatic <block singleton>` -> `getfield uu.bn:I` (raw block id) -> literal <veinSize> -> `invokespecial fl.<init>(II)V` -> `invokevirtual fl.a(World, Random, x, y, z)Z`.
orePopulationRules.constructorArgumentOrder: (rawBlockId, veinSize) - the first argument comes from the block's raw id field and the second is the literal vein size, e.g. fl.<init>(16, 32) for coal with vein size 32.
orePopulationRules.coordinateOffsets: x = chunkX*16 + Random.nextInt(16), z = chunkZ*16 + Random.nextInt(16) using the generator's own RNG seeded per chunk; y is drawn per rule below.

perSiteGroundTruth.idNote: block field literal read directly from the instruction stream

literalsBeforeEachSite.note: All integer literals pushed between the previous generator allocation site and each `new fl`, in instruction order. These are the raw evidence for attempts-per-chunk, vein size and height bound at each site.

perSiteReading.rule: Within each site's literal list the last-but-one value is the attempts-per-chunk loop bound (pushed by a small literal immediately before the nextInt(yRange) call, consumed as Random.nextInt(attempts)) and the last value is the literal vein size passed to fl.<init>. The 128/64/32/16 value is the nextInt argument that bounds y.
perSiteReading.workedExample_fl1: literals 0 (offset 496) and 20 (offset 501) are the loop's y-bound and attempts; 128 (offset 524) is the y draw bound and 16 (offset 538) is the vein size; the earlier 32 (offset 467) belongs to the preceding generator call site.

oreIdentification.confidence: HIGH for vein sizes, attempt counts and height bounds (literals read at verified instruction offsets). MEDIUM for which ore name belongs to which field name (see fieldNameMappingCaveat); the discriminating evidence is the constructor literal of the block singleton, which is (16,34) for coal, (15,33) for iron, (14,32) for gold, (21,160) for lapis, and texture-family indices 32/33/34/48/51/160 for the ore set.
oreIdentification.unresolved: The eight fl sites do not cover dirt in this verified method: the literal (3, 2) dirt singleton is not among the eight site block operands captured here, and the ninth fl-like allocation that would carry a 32-block vein with 20 attempts was not enumerated. Dirt generation is therefore present in the jar but its exact site attribution in this populate method remains unresolved and must not be asserted from this file.

decorationAndStructurePresence.note: Presence follows from the verified 23 allocation sites of yf.a(Lcl;II)V plus each generator class's own referenced constants.

springs.detail: No dedicated spring/waterfall generator class was identified among the 23 allocation sites of the verified populate method. Springs may be produced inside the terrain pass or inside a generator that does not appear as a `new` allocation in this method. Spring presence and rates are NOT established by this file.

unknowns: Springs/waterfalls: presence and rates not established.
Dirt: a dirt singleton (literal [3, 2]) exists in the registry, but no fl site in the verified populate method carries it; dirt generation site attribution is unresolved.
Field-name to raw-id pairing derived from the uu.<clinit> assignment sequence proved fragile (one off-by-one observed); ore names rest primarily on constructor literals and texture-index families.
Biome-conditioned variation (which biome enables which decoration) lives in the World/BiomeDecorator path and was not enumerated.
The non-overworld generator jd was identified but deliberately not analysed; no non-overworld numbers are claimed.

Attempts-per-chunk for each site are read from the literal immediately preceding each nextInt(yRange) call; the injection of that literal as Random.nextInt's argument was not simulated on the operand stack for every site, so attempt counts are HIGH but not machine-proved per site.
Saved-id versus raw-constructor-id equivalence for blocks is asserted only for the raw registry index; persistence mapping needs separate verification.

handoffForParent.whatThisSupports: A bounded Beta 1.7.3 generation-content profile can be specified from primary artifact evidence: per-ore vein sizes, attempts per chunk and height bounds; dungeon/lake/tree/flower/plant/clay generator identities; the raw block-id registry needed to express those rules as declarative data.
handoffForParent.whatThisDoesNotSupport: No terrain/noise/climate reconstruction, no spring claim, no dirt site attribution, no biome-conditioned decoration table, no saved-id mapping, no implementation.
handoffForParent.requiredIndependentVerification: The parent must independently re-run the artifact verification and at least one extraction command, and re-derive the ore literal table, before accepting these numbers. Accepted provided facts are not reliable until then.
